cve_summary: drivers/net/can/usb/gs_usb.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x and 4.10.x before 4.10.2 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash or memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a DMA scatterlist.
commit_message:
can: gs_usb: Don't use stack memory for USB transfers

Fixes: 05ca5270005c can: gs_usb: add ethtool set_phys_id callback to locate physical device

The gs_usb driver is performing USB transfers using buffers allocated on
the stack. This causes the driver to not function with vmapped stacks.
Instead, allocate memory for the transfer buffers.

Signed-off-by: Ethan Zonca <e@ethanzonca.com>
Cc: linux-stable <stable@vger.kernel.org> # >= v4.8
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
docstring:
Summary: This code fragment defines a USB disconnect handler and a USB device ID table for a driver managing USB devices.

Parameters: 
N/A

Returns: 
N/A

Logic: The `gs_usb_disconnect` function is called when a USB device is disconnected. It retrieves the device structure associated with the interface and sets the interface data to NULL. If the device structure is not found, it logs an error message and exits. The function then iterates through the device's channels, destroying each one, and kills any submitted USB requests before freeing the device structure. The USB device ID table defines supported USB devices by specifying their vendor and product IDs, with a terminating entry to mark the end of the list. This structure allows the driver to identify compatible devices during the connection process.
extraction_reason: vulnerable-side scope spans 3 top-level constructs (functions/declarations), not a single function
